newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Speculation pokes its head out IPO window.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Speculation pokes its head out IPO window.

text.p: Speculation is creeping into the resurgent market for initial public offerings, worrying some analysts that a drive for short-term gains could undermine overall market stability.
There has been a spirited rally in IPOs over the past few weeks, with mostly careful pricing and calm, healthy gains.
But Friday, Great Plains Software stunned new issues experts with a 102 percent jump at its debut.

"This is a market that makes you sweat," said David Menlow, president of the IPO Financial Network, referring to Great Plains' rocket ride. "It's a great company, with great underwriters, a great product and a great sector ... But this is just not sane IPO activity," he said.

Analysts said the "Goldman touch" of lead underwriter Goldman Sachs helped Great Plains, but they remained skeptical about its exuberant valuation level. The stock jumped 16-3/8 to close at 32-3/8 from an IPO price of $16.
This week again promises strong gains for investors who can buy into IPOs, with over 20 firms coming public, many from prestigious underwriting teams.
One of the hottest deals in the works this week is Qwest Communications, analysts say.
"Qwest could blow the doors off...It could even rise five, especially if the Dow continues to crawl into new territory," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

Qwest is building a nationwide fiber optic network for phone, fax, and communications that piggybacks on railroad lines. It started as part of Southern Pacific Rail Corp, now part of Union Pacific Corp. GTE Corp, Frontier Corp, and WorldCom Inc have all bought rights to use Qwest's network.
Qwest will offer 11.5 million shares for $17 and $20 each in an IPO to be led by Salomon Brothers.

Domain Energy Corp and Quinenco SA , a Chilean holding company for the Luksic Industrial Group, could also be hot, analysts say. Luksic owns stakes in copper products Madeco and brewer Compaa Cerveceras Unidas.
Other deals that could gain are Cal Dive International and the global offering of China plastics and resins-maker Beijing Yanua Petrochemical Co Ltd, scheduled to begin trading Monday morning.
David Menlow also says demand should drive up JLK Direct Distribution Inc JLK.N and 800-JR Cigar Inc at their openings.

Three Smith Barney offerings also look poised for slim gains: heating/air conditioning company Comfort Systems USA Inc; Coinstar, a maker of automatic coin counting machines, and international phone company Telegroup.

One analyst said gains for the deal should wash away some residue left after the Smith Barney-led IPO of virtual supermarket Peapod Inc, which went public at $16 a share, popped higher, and quickly slipped.

"On Wall Street, you're only as good as your last trade," he said. There have also been some negative reports in a trade publication on Comfort and Coinstar, but the worry may be unfounded with demand for at such strong levels for stock in both IPOs and secondary offerings.

Michael Klein, a managing director and head of the financial entrepreneurs group at Smith Barney, said so far the company is having no problem selling shares of Furniture Brands International in an 11 million offering, even though the company's largest stockholder, Apollo Investment Fund LP, is completely cashing out its stake.

"The story is strong enough that as they went on the roadshow, the stock went up to 16 and 17 despite the buyout structure," Klein said. When the company first said it planned to sell shares, it expected to sell for $15.875. The shares closed Friday at 16-7/8.
Ryan Jacob, director of research for the IPO Value Monitor, expects moderate to heavy volume for the next two weeks, but said activity could slow for the summer after the Fourth of July holiday.
"The performance is pretty strong and broad. And it's coming across many different sectors, not just one industry," he said.
((Wall Street Desk 212 859-1881))
